description: Abstract $Id: JointDistributionLebesgueQuadratures.tex,v 1.55 2020/11/30 15:49:52 mal Exp $ An important application of Lebesgue integral quadrature Malyshkin 2018 is developed. Given two random processes, f ⁡ ( x ) f(x) and g ⁡ ( x ) g(x) , two generalized eigenvalue problems can be formulated and solved.

title: What Can (and Can’t) we Do with Sparse Polynomials? DOI: 10.1145/3208976.3209027 ISBN: 978-1-4503-5550-6/18/07 Conference: 2018 ACM International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic Computation; July 16–19, 2018; New York, NY, USA ISSAC ’18: 2018 ACM International Symposium on Symbolic and Algebraic
creator: Daniel S. Roche
description: Abstract . Simply put, a sparse polynomial is one whose zero coefficients are not explicitly stored. Such objects are ubiquitous in exact computing, and so naturally we would like to have efficient algorithms to handle them. However, with this compact storage comes new algorithmic challenges, as fast algorithms for dense polynomials may no longer be efficient.

title: Relations between Schoenberg Coefficients on Real and Complex Spheres of Different Dimensions
creator: Pier Giovanni BISSIRI †, Valdir A. MENEGATTO ‡ and Emilio PORCU †§
description: Abstract Positive definite functions on spheres have received an increasing interest in many branches of mathematics and statistics. In particular, the Schoenberg sequences in the spectral representation of positive definite functions have been studied by several mathematicians in the last years.

title: A Flux-Balanced Fluid Model for Collisional Plasma Edge Turbulence: Model Derivation and Basic Physical Features
creator: Andrew J. Majda, Di Qi, Antoine J. Cerfon
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Andrew J. Majda, Di Qi, Antoine J. Cerfon. We propose a new reduced fluid model for the study of the drift wave – zonal flow dynamics in magnetically confined plasmas. Our model can be viewed as an extension of the classic Hasegawa-Wakatani (HW) model, and is based on an improved treatment of the electron dynamics parallel to the field lines, to guarantee a balanced electron flux on the magnetic surfaces.

title: Sparse space-time models: Concentration Inequalities and Lasso
creator: G. Ost ??, P. Reynaud-Bouret ??
description: Abstract Inspired by Kalikow-type decompositions, we introduce a new stochastic model of infinite neuronal networks, for which we establish sharp oracle inequalities for Lasso methods and restricted eigenvalue properties for the associated Gram matrix with high probability. These results hold even if the network is only partially observed.

title: From Bare Metal to Virtual Conference: Practice and Experience in Advanced Research Computing; July 22–26, 2018; Pittsburgh, PA, USA PEARC ’18: Practice and Experience in Advanced Research Computing, July 22–26, 2018, Pittsburgh, PA, USA DOI: 10.1145/3219104.3219164 ISBN: 978-1-4503-6446-1/18/07 CCS
creator: Evan F. Bollig, James C. Wilgenbusch
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Evan F. Bollig, James C. Wilgenbusch. As primary provider for research computing services at the University of Minnesota, the Minnesota Supercomputing Institute (MSI) has long been responsible for serving the needs of a user-base numbering in the thousands. In recent years, MSI—like many other HPC centers—has observed a growing need for self-service, on-demand, data-intensive research, as well as the emergence of many new controlled-access datasets for research purposes.

title: Hecke Operators on Vector-Valued Modular Forms This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Moonshine and String Theory. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/moonshine.html
creator: Vincent BOUCHARD †, Thomas CREUTZIG †‡ and Aniket JOSHI †
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Vincent BOUCHARD †, Thomas CREUTZIG †‡ and Aniket JOSHI †. We study Hecke operators on vector-valued modular forms for the Weil representation ρ L \rho_{L} of a lattice L L . We first construct Hecke operators 𝒯 r \mathcal{T}_{r} that map vector-valued modular forms of type ρ L \rho_{L} into vector-valued modular forms of type ρ L ⁡ ( r ) \rho_{L(r)} , where L ⁡ ( r ) L(r) is the lattice L L with rescaled bilinear form ( ⋅ , ⋅ )

title: Learning to Play Pong using Policy Gradient Learning
creator: Somnuk Phon-Amnuaisuk
description: Abstract Activities in reinforcement learning (RL) revolve around learning the Markov decision process (MDP) model, in particular, the following parameters: state values, V V ; state-action values, Q Q ; and policy, π \pi . These parameters are commonly implemented as an array.

title: Leveraging OpenStack and Ceph for a Controlled-Access Data Cloud Conference: Practice and Experience in Advanced Research Computing; July 22–26, 2018; Pittsburgh, PA, USA PEARC ’18: Practice and Experience in Advanced Research Computing, July 22–26, 2018, Pittsburgh, PA, USA DOI: 10.1145/3219104.321
creator: Evan F. Bollig, Graham T. Allan, Benjamin J. Lynch, Yectli A. Huerta, Mathew Mix, Edward A. Munsell, Raychel M. Benson, Brent Swartz
description: Abstract . While traditional HPC has and continues to satisfy most workflows, a new generation of researchers has emerged looking for sophisticated, scalable, on-demand, and self-service control of compute infrastructure in a cloud-like environment. Many also seek safe harbors to operate on or store sensitive and/or controlled-access data in a high capacity environment.

title: Edge modes in 1D microwave photonic crystal
creator: Aleksey Girich, Liubov Ivzhenko, Ganna Kharchenko, Sergey Polevoy, Sergey Tarapov, Maciej Krawczyk, Jarosław W. Kłos
description: Abstract The microstrip of modulated width is a realization of a one-dimensional photonic crystal operating in the microwave regime. Like any photonic crystal, the periodic microstrip is characterised by the presence of frequency bands and band gaps that enable and prohibit wave propagation, respectively.

title: Domain Generalization via Conditional Invariant Representations
creator: Ya Li, Mingming Gong, Xinmei Tian, Tongliang Liu, Dacheng Tao
description: Abstract Domain generalization aims to apply knowledge gained from multiple labeled source domains to unseen target domains. The main difficulty comes from the dataset bias: training data and test data have different distributions, and the training set contains heterogeneous samples from different distributions. Let X X denote the features, and Y Y be the class labels.

title: A strategy for a general search for new phenomena using data-derived signal regions and its application within the ATLAS experiment
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by . This paper describes a strategy for a general search used by the ATLAS Collaboration to find potential indications of new physics. Events are classified according to their final state into many event classes. For each event class an automated search algorithm tests whether the data are compatible with the Monte Carlo simulated expectation in several distributions sensitive to the effects of new physics. The significance of a deviation is quantified using pseudo-experiments.

title: Heat-Bath Algorithmic Cooling with optimal thermalization strategies
creator: Álvaro M. Alhambra, Matteo Lostaglio, Christopher Perry
description: Abstract Heat-Bath Algorithmic Cooling is a set of techniques for producing highly pure quantum systems by utilizing a surrounding heat-bath and unitary interactions. These techniques originally used the thermal environment only to fully thermalize ancillas at the environment temperature. Here we extend HBAC protocols by optimizing over the thermalization strategy.

title: Linear superposition as a core theorem of quantum empiricism
creator: Yurii V. Brezhnev ∗
description: Abstract . Clarifying the nature of the quantum state | 𝚿 ⟩ |\boldsymbol{\Psi}\rangle is at the root of the problems with insight into counter-intuitive quantum postulates. We provide a direct—and math-axiom free—empirical derivation of this object as an element of a vector space.

title: Lesion segmentation using U-Net network
creator: Adrien Motsch, Sébastien Motsch, Thibaut Saguet
description: Abstract This paper explains the method used in the segmentation challenge (Task 1) in the International Skin Imaging Collaboration’s (ISIC) Skin Lesion Analysis Towards Melanoma Detection challenge held in 2018. We have trained a U-Net network to perform the segmentation.

title: On a Potential Game-theoretic Approach to Event-triggered Distributed Resource Allocation
creator: Prashant Bansode, Sharad Jadhav, Mukesh Patil, Navdeep Singh
description: Abstract This paper proposes a potential game theoretic approach to address event-triggered distributed resource allocation in multi-agent systems. The fitness dynamic of the population is proposed and exploited as a linear parameter-varying dynamic to achieve the event-triggered distributed resource allocation. Firstly, it is shown that the dynamic resembles a consensus protocol and is equivalent to the replicator dynamic.

title: Skin Lesion Segmentation Using Atrous Convolution via DeepLab v3
creator: Yujie Wang - Troy High School, MI, wangyuji431@gmail.com, Simon Sun - Harvard College, ssun@college.harvard.eduJahow Yu - Troy High School, MI, jahowyu@gmail.comDr. Limin Yu - Beaumont Health, limin.yu@beaumont.edu
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Yujie Wang - Troy High School, MI, wangyuji431@gmail.com, Simon Sun - Harvard College, ssun@college.harvard.eduJahow Yu - Troy High School, MI, jahowyu@gmail.comDr. Limin Yu - Beaumont Health, limin.yu@beaumont.edu. As melanoma diagnoses increase across the US, automated efforts to identify malignant lesions become increasingly of interest to the research community. Segmentation of dermoscopic images is the first step in this process, thus accuracy is crucial.

title: Undecidability of a weak version of mso + U
creator: Mikołaj Bojańczyk, Laure Daviaud, Bruno Guillon, Vincent Penelle, A. V. Sreejith
description: Abstract . We prove the undecidability of mso on ω \omega -words extended with the second-order predicate U 1 \texttt{U}_{1} ( X ) \left(X\right) which says that the distance between consecutive positions in a set X ⊆ ℕ X\subseteq\mathbb{N} is unbounded.

title: Effective Reformulation of Query for Code Search using Crowdsourced Knowledge and Extra-Large Data Analytics
creator: Mohammad Masudur Rahman Chanchal K. Roy
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Mohammad Masudur Rahman Chanchal K. Roy. Software developers frequently issue generic natural language queries for code search while using code search engines (e.g., GitHub native search, Krugle). Such queries often do not lead to any relevant results due to vocabulary mismatch problems. In this paper, we propose a novel technique that automatically identifies relevant and specific API classes from Stack Overflow Q & A site for a programming task written as a natural language query, and then reformulates the query for improved code search.

title: Laser and Radio Tracking for Planetary Science Missions - A Comparison
creator: Dominic Dirkx, Ivan Prochazka, Sven Bauer, Pieter Visser, Ron Noomen, Leonid I. Gurvits, Bert Vermeersen
description: Abstract At present, tracking data for planetary missions largely consists of radio observables: range-rate (Doppler), range and angular position (VLBI/ Δ \Delta DOR). Future planetary missions may use Interplanetary Laser Ranging (ILR) as a tracking observable. Two-way ILR will provide range data that are about 2 orders of magnitude more accurate than radio-based range data.

title: Analysis of Logarithmic Amortised Complexity
creator: Martin Hofmann † {\dagger}, Georg Moser
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Martin Hofmann † {\dagger}, Georg Moser. We introduce a novel amortised resource analysis based on a potential-based type system. This type system gives rise to logarithmic and polynomial bounds on the runtime complexity and is the first such system to exhibit logarithmic amortised complexity. We relate the thus obtained automatable amortised resource analysis to manual amortised analyses of self-adjusting data structures, like splay trees, that can be found in the literature.

title: Talent Flow Analytics in Online Professional Network
creator: Richard J. Oentaryo, Ee-Peng Lim, Xavier Jayaraj Siddarth Ashok, Philips Kokoh Prasetyo, Koon Han Ong † \dagger, Zi Quan Lau † \dagger
description: Abstract Analyzing job hopping behavior is important for understanding job preference and career progression of working individuals. When analyzed at the workforce population level, job hop analysis helps to gain insights of talent flow among different jobs and organizations. Traditionally, surveys are conducted on job seekers and employers to study job hop behavior.

title: Search for charged Higgs bosons decaying via H ± → τ ± ​ ν τ H^{\pm}\to\tau^{\pm}\nu_{\tau} in the τ \tau +jets and τ \tau +lepton final states with 36 fb − 1 {\mathrm{fb}^{-1}} of p ​ p pp collision data recorded at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS experiment
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract Charged Higgs bosons produced either in top-quark decays or in association with a top-quark, subsequently decaying via H ± → τ ± ​ ν τ H^{\pm}\to\tau^{\pm}\nu_{\tau} , are searched for in 36.1 fb − 1 {\mathrm{fb}^{-1}} of proton–proton collision data at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV recorded with the ATLAS detector.

title: Every square can be tiled with T-tetrominos and no more than 5 monominos
creator: Jack Grahl
description: Abstract If n n is a multiple of 4, then a square of side n n can be tiled with T-tetrominos, using a well-known construction. If n n is even but not a multiple of four, then there exists an equally well-known construction for tiling a square of side n n with T-tetrominos and exactly 4 monominos.

title: Primal-Dual Gradient Flow Algorithm for Distributed Support Vector Machines
creator: Prashant Bansode, Sushant Bahadure, Navdeep Singh
description: Abstract In this paper, a primal-dual gradient flow algorithm for distributed support vector machines (DSVM) is proposed. A network of computing nodes, each carrying a subset of horizontally partitioned large dataset is considered. The nodes are represented as dynamical systems with Arrow-Hurwicz-Uzawa gradient flow dynamics, derived from the Lagrangian function of the DSVM problem.

title: Bipolar thermoelectric effects in semiconducting carbon nanotubes: Description in terms of one-dimensional Dirac electrons
creator: Takahiro Yamamoto 1 and Hidetoshi Fukuyama 2
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Takahiro Yamamoto 1 and Hidetoshi Fukuyama 2. The thermoelectric effects in semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are investigated based on the linear response theory combined with the thermal Green’s function method. It is shown that the electronic states near the lowest conduction band minimum and the highest valence band maximum can be effectively described in terms of one-dimensional (1D) Dirac electrons to which a theoretical scheme is developed to describe the thermoelectric responses making it possible to study the effects of inter-band impurity scattering

title: How to estimate the entropy inside a Schwarzschild black hole
creator: Thomas Schürmann
description: Abstract We reconsider the interrelation between the Schwarzschild radius and mass of a spherical symmetric non-rotating and uncharged black hole. By applying the relativistic mass-energy equivalence, the area of the horizon is expressed independently of the Schwarzschild radius in terms of an occupation number operator corresponding to the underlying many-body system of the particles inside the black hole.

title: End-to-End Deep Imitation Learning: Robot Soccer Case Study
creator: Okan Aşık, Binnur Görer, H. Levent Akın
description: Abstract In imitation learning, behavior learning is generally done using the features extracted from the demonstration data. Recent deep learning algorithms enable the development of machine learning methods that can get high dimensional data as an input. In this work, we use imitation learning to teach the robot to dribble the ball to the goal.

title: Encoderless Gimbal Calibration of Dynamic Multi-Camera Clusters
creator: Christopher L. Choi, Jason Rebello, Leonid Koppel, Pranav Ganti, Arun Das, Steven L. Waslander
description: Abstract Dynamic Camera Clusters (DCCs) are multi-camera systems where one or more cameras are mounted on actuated mechanisms such as a gimbal. Existing methods for DCC calibration rely on joint angle measurements to resolve the time-varying transformation between the dynamic and static camera.

title: Automatically Assessing Vulnerabilities Discovered by Compositional Analysis Conference: International Workshop on Machine Learning and Software Engineering in Symbiosis; September 2018; Montpellier, France CCS: Security and privacy Vulnerability management CCS: Software and its engineering Software
creator: Saahil Ognawala, Ricardo Nales Amato, Alexander Pretschner, Pooja Kulkarni
description: Abstract . Testing is the most widely employed method to find vulnerabilities in real-world software programs. Compositional analysis, based on symbolic execution, is an automated testing method to find vulnerabilities in medium- to large-scale programs consisting of many interacting components. However, existing compositional analysis frameworks do not assess the severity of reported vulnerabilities.

title: The Soft Multivariate Truncated Normal Distribution with Applications to Bayesian Constrained Estimation
creator: Allyson Souris, Anirban Bhattacharya, Debdeep Pati, Department of Statistics, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX
description: Abstract Abstract. We propose a new distribution, called the soft tMVN distribution, which provides a smooth approximation to the truncated multivariate normal (tMVN) distribution with linear constraints. An efficient blocked Gibbs sampler is developed to sample from the soft tMVN distribution in high dimensions.

title: Deep Global Model Reduction Learning
creator: Siu Wun Cheung, Eric T. Chung, Yalchin Efendiev, Eduardo Gildin, Yating Wang
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Siu Wun Cheung, Eric T. Chung, Yalchin Efendiev, Eduardo Gildin, Yating Wang. In this paper, we combine deep learning concepts and some proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) model reduction methods for predicting flow in heterogeneous porous media. Nonlinear flow dynamics is studied, where the dynamics is regarded as a multi-layer network. The solution at the current time step is regarded as a multi-layer network of the solution at the initial time and input parameters.

title: Multi-Resolution Networks for Semantic Segmentation in Whole Slide Images
creator: Feng Gu, Nikolay Burlutskiy, Mats Andersson, Lena Kajland Wilén
description: Abstract Digital pathology provides an excellent opportunity for applying fully convolutional networks (FCNs) to tasks, such as semantic segmentation of whole slide images (WSIs). However, standard FCNs face challenges with respect to multi-resolution, inherited from the pyramid arrangement of WSIs. As a result, networks specifically designed to learn and aggregate information at different levels are desired.

title: A Convex Formulation for Binary Tomography
creator: Ajinkya Kadu, Tristan van Leeuwen
description: Abstract Binary tomography is concerned with the recovery of binary images from a few of their projections (i.e., sums of the pixel values along various directions). To reconstruct an image from noisy projection data, one can pose it as a constrained least-squares problem.

title: Full counting statistics and large deviations in thermal 1D Bose gas
creator: Maksims Arzamasovs, Dimitri M. Gangardt
description: Abstract We obtain the distribution of number of atoms in an interval (full counting statistics) of Lieb-Liniger model of interacting bosons in one dimension. Our results are valid in the weakly interacting regime in a parametrically large window of temperatures and interval lengths.

title: Multiple sclerosis lesion enhancement and white matter region estimation using hyperintensities in FLAIR images
creator: Paulo G. de Lima Freire, Ricardo J. Ferrari
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Paulo G. de Lima Freire, Ricardo J. Ferrari. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a demyelinating disease that affects more than 2 million people worldwide. The most used imaging technique to help in its diagnosis and follow-up is magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) images are usually acquired in the context of MS because lesions often appear hyperintense in this particular image weight, making it easier for physicians to identify them.

title: Arun Uday
description: Abstract ﻿ \setlistdepth 9 A dual identity based symbolic understanding of the Gödel’s incompleteness theorems, P-NP problem, Zeno’s paradox and Continuum Hypothesis Abstract: A semantic analysis of formal systems is undertaken, wherein the duality of their symbolic definition based on the `` State of Doing " and `` State of Being " is brought out.

title: Regulation of T cell expansion by antigen presentation dynamics
creator: Andreas Mayer, Yaojun Zhang, Alan S. Perelson, Ned S. Wingreen
description: Abstract An essential feature of the adaptive immune system is the proliferation of antigen-specific lymphocytes during an immune reaction to form a large pool of effector cells. This proliferation must be regulated to ensure an effective response to infection while avoiding immunopathology.

title: Jellium and Cell Model for Titratable Colloids with Continuous Size Distribution
creator: Guillaume Bareigts, Christophe Labbez
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Guillaume Bareigts, Christophe Labbez. A good understanding and determination of colloidal interactions is paramount to comprehend and model the thermodynamic and structural properties of colloidal suspensions. In concentrated aqueous suspensions of colloids with a titratable surface charge, this determination is, however, complicated by the density dependence of the effective pair potential due to both the many-body interactions and the charge regulation of the colloids. In addition, colloids generally present a size distribution which results in a virtually infinite combination of colloid pairs.

title: A ϕ \phi -Competitive Algorithm for Scheduling Packets with Deadlines A preliminary version of this article first appeared in SODA’19 [ 22 ] . An extended and thoroughly revised version was then published in SIAM Journal on Computing [ 23 ] , with Copyright transferred to SIAM. This version, with ad
creator: Pavel Veselý, Marek Chrobak, Łukasz Jeż, Jiří Sgall
description: Abstract In the online packet scheduling problem with deadlines ( PacketSchD , for short), the goal is to schedule transmissions of packets that arrive over time in a network switch and need to be sent across a link. Each packet has a deadline, representing its urgency, and a non-negative weight, that represents its priority.

title: Anomaly detection in static networks using egonets
creator: Srijan Sengupta
description: Abstract Abstract: Network data has rapidly emerged as an important and active area of statistical methodology. In this paper we consider the problem of anomaly detection in networks. Given a large background network, we seek to detect whether there is a small anomalous subgraph present in the network, and if such a subgraph is present, which nodes constitute the subgraph.

title: Minimum supports of functions on the Hamming graphs with spectral constraints Thanks: The reported study was funded by RFBR according to the research project 18-31-00126
creator: Alexandr Valyuzhenich, Konstantin Vorob’ev
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Alexandr Valyuzhenich, Konstantin Vorob’ev. We study functions defined on the vertices of the Hamming graphs H ⁡ ( n , q ) H(n,q) . The adjacency matrix of H ⁡ ( n , q ) H(n,q) has n + 1 n+1 distinct eigenvalues n ⁡ ( q − 1 ) − q ⋅ i n(q-1)-q\cdot i with corresponding eigenspaces U i ​ ( n , q ) U_{i}(n,q) for 0 ≤ i ≤ n 0\leq i\leq n .

title: The Time-SIFT method : detecting 3-D changes from archival photogrammetric analysis with almost exclusively image information
creator: D. Feurer, F. Vinatier
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by D. Feurer, F. Vinatier. Archival aerial imagery is a source of worldwide very high resolution data for documenting paste 3-D changes. However, external information is required so that accurate 3-D models can be computed from archival aerial imagery. In this research, we propose and test a new method, termed Time-SIFT (Scale Invariant Feature Transform), which allows for computing coherent multi-temporal Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) with almost exclusively image information.

title: Vulnerable to Misinformation? Verifi! DOI: 10.475/123_4 ISBN: 123-4567-24-567/08/06 Conference: ACM Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces; March 2019; Los Angeles, California USA 4 Price: 15.00 Conference: 24th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces; March 17–20, 2019; Marina de
creator: Alireza Karduni Isaac Cho Ryan Wesslen Sashank Santhanam, Svitlana Volkova Dustin L Arendt, Samira Shaikh Wenwen Dou
description: Abstract . We present Verifi2, a visual analytic system to support the investigation of misinformation on social media. Various models and studies have emerged from multiple disciplines to detect or understand the effects of misinformation. However, there is still a lack of intuitive and accessible tools that help social media users distinguish misinformation from verified news.

title: Axion mass prediction from minimal grand unification
creator: Luca Di Luzio, Andreas Ringwald, Carlos Tamarit
description: Abstract We propose a minimal realization of the Peccei Quinn mechanism in a realistic SU(5) model, where the axion mass is directly connected to the grand-unification scale. By taking into account constraints from proton decay, collider searches and gauge coupling unification, we predict the axion mass: m a ∈ [ 4.8 , 6.6 ] m_{a}\in[4.8,6.6] neV.

title: An Affective Robot Companion for Assisting the Elderly in a Cognitive Game Scenario
creator: Nikhil Churamani, Alexander Sutherland and Pablo Barros
description: Abstract Being able to recognize emotions in human users is considered a highly desirable trait in HRI ( HRI ) scenarios. However, most contemporary approaches rarely attempt to apply recognized emotional features in an active manner to modulate robot decision-making and dialogue for the benefit of the user.

title: Constant-Delay Enumeration for Nondeterministic Document Spanners
creator: Antoine Amarilli, Pierre Bourhis, Stefan Mengel, Matthias Niewerth
description: Abstract We consider the information extraction framework known as document spanners , and study the problem of efficiently computing the results of the extraction from an input document, where the extraction task is described as a sequential variable-set automaton (VA).

title: Wasserstein metric-driven Bayesian inversion with applications to signal processing
creator: M. Motamed, D. Appelö
description: Abstract Abstract. We present a Bayesian framework based on a new exponential likelihood function driven by the quadratic Wasserstein metric. Compared to conventional Bayesian models based on Gaussian likelihood functions driven by the least-squares norm ( L_{2} norm), the new framework features several advantages.

title: Search for Higgs bosons produced via vector-boson fusion and decaying into bottom quark pairs in s = 13 TeV \sqrt{s}=$13\text{\,}\mathrm{TeV}$ p ​ p pp collisions with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for the b ​ b ¯ b\bar{b} decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson produced through vector-boson fusion is presented. Three mutually exclusive channels are considered: two all-hadronic channels and a photon-associated channel. Results are reported from the analysis of up to 30.6 fb − 1 30.

title: Dark Neutrino Portal to Explain MiniBooNE excess Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-18-336-T
creator: Enrico Bertuzzo, Sudip Jana, Pedro A. N. Machado, Renata Zukanovich Funchal
description: Abstract We present a novel framework that provides an explanation to the long-standing excess of electron-like events in the MiniBooNE experiment at Fermilab. We suggest a new dark sector containing a dark neutrino and a dark gauge boson, both with masses between a few tens and a few hundreds of MeV.

title: Adaptive, locally-linear models of complex dynamics
creator: Antonio C. Costa a , Tosif Ahamed b , Greg J. Stephens a,b
description: Abstract The dynamics of complex systems generally include high dimensional, nonstationary and nonlinear behavior, all of which pose fundamental challenges to quantitative understanding. To address these difficulties we detail a new approach based on local linear models within windows determined adaptively from data.

title: Vanishing trace anomaly in flat spacetime
creator: Zygmunt Lalak, Paweł Olszewski
description: Abstract Quantum scale invariant regularization is a variant of dimensional regularization where the renormalization scale is treated as a dynamical field. But, rather than be regarded as a novel regularization method on par with dimensional regularization, momentum cutoff, Pauli-Villars etc.

title: Fault-tolerant gates via homological product codes
creator: Tomas Jochym-O’Connor
description: Abstract A method for the implementation of a universal set of fault-tolerant logical gates is presented using homological product codes. In particular, it is shown that one can fault-tolerantly map between different encoded representations of a given logical state, enabling the application of different classes of transversal gates belonging to the underlying quantum codes.

title: Adaptive Body Area Networks Using Kinematics and Biosignals
creator: Ali Moin, Arno Thielens, Alvaro Araujo, Alberto Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, Jan M. Rabaey
description: Abstract The increasing penetration of wearable and implantable devices necessitates energy-efficient and robust ways of connecting them to each other and to the cloud. However, the wireless channel around the human body poses unique challenges such as a high and variable path-loss caused by frequent changes in the relative node positions as well as the surrounding environment.

title: General-purpose tagging of Freesound audio with AudioSet labels: Task Description, Dataset, and Baseline
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by . This paper describes Task 2 of the DCASE 2018 Challenge, titled “General-purpose audio tagging of Freesound content with AudioSet labels”. This task was hosted on the Kaggle platform as “Freesound General-Purpose Audio Tagging Challenge”. The goal of the task is to build an audio tagging system that can recognize the category of an audio clip from a subset of 41 diverse categories drawn from the AudioSet Ontology. We present the task, the dataset prepared for the competition, and a baseline system.

title: Search for Higgs boson pair production in the γ ​ γ ​ W ​ W ∗ \gamma\gamma WW^{*} channel using p ​ p pp collision data recorded at s \sqrt{s} = = 13 TeV 13\text{\,}\mathrm{TeV} with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract Searches for non-resonant and resonant Higgs boson pair production are performed in the γ ​ γ ​ W ​ W ∗ \gamma\gamma WW^{*} channel with the final state of γ ​ γ ​ ℓ ​ ν ​ j ​ j \gamma\gamma\ell\nu jj using 36.1 fb − 1 36.

title: Strain-engineered Majorana Zero Energy Modes and φ 0 \varphi_{0} Josephson State in Black Phosphorus
creator: Mohammad Alidoust, Morten Willatzen, Antti-Pekka Jauho
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Mohammad Alidoust, Morten Willatzen, Antti-Pekka Jauho. We develop a theory for strain control of Majorana zero energy modes and the Josephson effect in black phosphorus (BP) devices proximity coupled to a superconductor. Employing realistic values for the band parameters subject to strain, we show that the strain closes the intrinsic band gap of BP; however, the proximity effect from the superconductor reopens it and creates Dirac and Weyl nodes.

title: Asymptotic Optimality of Mixture Rules for Detecting Changes in General Stochastic Models Thanks: The work was supported in part by the Russian Federation 5-100 program, the Russian Federation Ministry of Science and Education Arctic program and the grant 18-19-00452 from the Russian Science Foundat
creator: Alexander G. Tartakovsky
description: Abstract The paper addresses a sequential changepoint detection problem for a general stochastic model, assuming that the observed data may be non-i.i.d. (i.e., dependent and non-identically distributed) and the prior distribution of the change point is arbitrary. Tartakovsky and Veeravalli (2005), Baron and Tartakovsky (2006), and, more recently, Tartakovsky (2017) developed a general asymptotic theory of changepoint detection for non-i.i.d.

title: Varying Driver Velocity Fields in Photospheric MHD Wave Simulations Varying Driver Velocity Fields in Photospheric MHD Wave Simulations – References
creator: A. J. Leonard, S. J. Mumford, V. Fedun, R. Erdélyi
description: Abstract Torsional motions are ubiquitous in the solar atmosphere. In this work, we perform 3D numerical simulations which mimic a vortex-type photospheric driver with a Gaussian spatial profile. This driver is implemented to excite MHD waves in an axially symmetric, 3D magnetic flux tube embedded in a realistic solar atmosphere.

title: PCach: The Case for Pre-Caching your Mobile Data
creator: Katia Jaffrès-Runser, Gentian Jakllari
description: Abstract We present PCach, a smartphone-based approach for relieving the congestion in cellular network resulting from the exponential growth in mobile data traffic. The basic idea underlying PCach is simple: use WiFi to proactively cache content on the smartphone’s memory, which otherwise would have been delivered through the cellular network.

title: IDEAL characterization of higher dimensional spherically symmetric black holes
creator: Igor Khavkine

title: Diffusion and consensus on weakly connected directed graphs
creator: J. J. P. Veerman, E. Kummel
description: Abstract Let G G be a weakly connected directed graph with asymmetric graph Laplacian ℒ {\cal L} . Consensus and diffusion are dual dynamical processes defined on G G by x ˙ = − ℒ ​ x \dot{x}=-{\cal L}x for consensus and p ˙ = − p ​ ℒ \dot{p}=-p{\cal L} for diffusion.

title: Term Set Expansion based on Multi-Context Term Embeddings: an End-to-end Workflow
creator: Jonathan Mamou, Oren Pereg, Moshe Wasserblat, Ido Dagan, Yoav Goldberg, Alon Eirew, Yael Green, Shira Guskin, Peter Izsak, Daniel Korat
description: Abstract 0 0 footnotetext: This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. License details: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . We present SetExpander, a corpus-based system for expanding a seed set of terms into a more complete set of terms that belong to the same semantic class. SetExpander implements an iterative end-to end workflow for term set expansion.

title: Transverse Momentum Spectra at Threshold for Groomed Heavy Quark Jets
creator: Yiannis Makris, Varun Vaidya
description: Abstract We present the transverse momentum spectrum for a heavy hadron at threshold in a groomed jet initiated by a heavy quark. The cross section is doubly differential in the energy fraction of an identified heavy hadron in the jet and its transverse momentum measured with respect to the groomed (recoil free) jet axis.

title: ASYMPTOTICALLY OPTIMAL QUICKEST CHANGE DETECTION IN MULTISTREAM DATA—PART 1: GENERAL STOCHASTIC MODELS
creator: Alexander G. Tartakovskylabel=e1]agt@phystech.edu t1
description: Abstract Assume that there are multiple data streams (channels, sensors) and in each stream the process of interest produces generally dependent and non-identically distributed observations. When the process is in a normal mode (in-control), the (pre-change) distribution is known, but when the process becomes abnormal there is a parametric uncertainty, i.e.

title: Open Source Automatic Speech Recognition for German
creator: Benjamin Milde, Arne Köhn
description: Abstract High quality Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is a prerequisite for speech-based applications and research. While state-of-the-art ASR software is freely available, the language dependent acoustic models are lacking for languages other than English, due to the limited amount of freely available training data.

title: Effects of Degradations on Deep Neural Network Architectures
creator: Prasun Roy, Subhankar Ghosh, Saumik Bhattacharya, and Umapada Pal, Senior member, IEEE Indian Statistical Institute Kolkata, India, https://github.com/prasunroy/cnn-on-degraded-images
description: Abstract Deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) have massively influenced recent advances in large-scale image classification. More recently, a dynamic routing algorithm with capsules (groups of neurons) has shown state-of-the-art recognition performance. However, the behavior of such networks in the presence of a degrading signal (noise) is mostly unexplored.

title: In situ calibration of large-radius jet energy and mass in 13 TeV proton–proton collisions with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract The response of the ATLAS detector to large-radius jets is measured in situ using 36.2 fb -1 of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV proton–proton collisions provided by the LHC and recorded by the ATLAS experiment during 2015 and 2016.

title: The FIRST Classifier: Compact and Extended Radio Galaxy Classification using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks 2018 The FIRST Classifier: Compact and Extended Radio Galaxy Classification using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks – References
creator: Wathela Alhassan, A.R. Taylor, Mattia Vaccari
description: Abstract Upcoming surveys with new radio observatories such as the Square Kilometer Array will generate a wealth of imaging data containing large numbers of radio galaxies. Different classes of radio galaxies can be used as tracers of the cosmic environment, including the dark matter density field, to address key cosmological questions.

title: A Style-Aware Content Loss for Real-time HD Style Transfer
creator: Artsiom Sanakoyeu, Dmytro Kotovenko, Sabine Lang, Björn Ommer
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Artsiom Sanakoyeu, Dmytro Kotovenko, Sabine Lang, Björn Ommer. Recently, style transfer has received a lot of attention. While much of this research has aimed at speeding up processing, the approaches are still lacking from a principled, art historical standpoint: a style is more than just a single image or an artist, but previous work is limited to only a single instance of a style or shows no benefit from more images.

title: Robustness of Magic and Symmetries of the Stabiliser Polytope
creator: Markus Heinrich, David Gross
description: Abstract We give a new algorithm for computing the robustness of magic —a measure of the utility of quantum states as a computational resource. Our work is motivated by the magic state model of fault-tolerant quantum computation. In this model, all unitaries belong to the Clifford group.

title: Deformations of Pre-Symplectic Structures: a Dirac Geometry Approach
creator: Florian SCHÄTZ † and Marco ZAMBON ‡
description: Abstract We explain the geometric origin of the L ∞ L_{\infty} -algebra controlling deformations of pre-symplectic structures. keywords pre-symplectic geometry; deformation theory; Dirac geometry AMS 17B70; 53D17; 58H15 † † shorttitle: Deformations of Pre-Symplectic Structures: a Dirac Geometry Approach † † runningauthor: F. title: The top-quark window on compositeness at future lepton colliders Preprint: DESY 18-114
creator: Gauthier Durieux, Oleksii Matsedonskyi
description: Abstract In composite Higgs (CH) models, large mixings between the top quark and the new strongly interacting sector are required to generate its sizeable Yukawa coupling. Precise measurements involving top as well as left-handed bottom quarks therefore offer an interesting opportunity to probe such new physics scenarios.

title: Global Existence and Ulam–Hyers Stability of Ψ \Psi –Hilfer Fractional Differential Equations
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the Cauchy-type problem for a nonlinear differential equation involving Ψ \Psi -Hilfer fractional derivative and prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions in the weighted space of functions. The Ulam–Hyers and Ulam–Hyers–Rassias stability of Cauchy–type problem is investigated via successive approximation method.

title: Low- and high-energy phenomenology of a doubly charged scalar Preprint: PSI-PR-18-08, ZU-TH-28/18
creator: Andreas Crivellin, Margherita Ghezzi, Luca Panizzi, Giovanni Marco Pruna, Adrian Signer
description: Abstract We explore the phenomenology of an S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) -singlet doubly charged scalar at the high and low energy frontier. Such a particle is predicted in different new physics models, like left-right symmetric models or the Zee–Babu model.

title: On the theory of high- T c T_{\text{c}} superconductivity of doped cuprates
creator: Y.G. Pogorelov ? {}^{\textsf{\footnotesize{\mbox{?}}}}, V.M. Loktev ? , ?
description: Abstract A theoretical analysis is presented on possible effects of disorder by dopants in high-temperature superconducting cuprate perovskites, to define their basic spectra of spin and electronic excitations, and the subsequent observable properties, especially doping dependence of superconducting order parameter.

title: Correcting symmetry imperfections in linear multipole traps
creator: J. Pedregosa-Gutierrez, C. Champenois, M. Houssin, M.R. Kamsap, M. Knoop
description: Abstract Résumé Multipole radio-frequency traps are central to collisional experiments in cryogenic environments. They also offer possibilities to generate new type of ion crystals topologies and in particular the potential to create infinite 1D/2D structures : ion rings and ion tubes.

title: How to capitalize on a priori contrasts in linear (mixed) models: A tutorial
creator: Daniel J. Schad 1, Shravan Vasishth 1, Sven Hohenstein 1, & Reinhold Kliegl 1
description: Abstract Factorial experiments in research on memory, language, and in other areas are often analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA). However, for effects with more than one numerator degrees of freedom, e.g., for experimental factors with more than two levels, the ANOVA omnibus F-test is not informative about the source of a main effect or interaction.

title: Global and local evaluation of link prediction tasks with neural embeddings
creator: Asan Agibetov, Matthias Samwald
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Asan Agibetov, Matthias Samwald. We focus our attention on the link prediction problem for knowledge graphs, which is treated herein as a binary classification task on neural embeddings of the entities. By comparing, combining and extending different methodologies for link prediction on graph-based data coming from different domains, we formalize a unified methodology for the quality evaluation benchmark of neural embeddings for knowledge graphs.

title: A Resolution of the Poisson Problem for Elastic Plates
creator: Francesca Da Lio, Francesco Palmurella*, Tristan Rivière*
description: Abstract The Poisson problem consists in finding an immersed surface Σ ⊂ ℝ m \Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^{m} minimising Germain’s elastic energy (known as Willmore energy in geometry) with prescribed boundary, boundary Gauss map and area. This problem represents a non-linear model for the equilibrium state of thin, clamped elastic plates originating from the work of S. Germain and S.D.

title: An experiment in distributed Internet address management using blockchains
creator: Stefano Angieri, Alberto García-Martínez, Bingyang Liu, Zhiwei Yan, Chuang Wang, Marcelo Bagnulo
description: Abstract The current system to manage the global pool of IP addresses is centralized in five transnational organizations, the Regional Internet Registries (RIRs). Each of these RIRs manage the address pool for a large number of countries. Because the RIRs are private organizations, they are subject to the legal framework of the country where they are based.

title: Enhanced deep detection of Raman scattered light by wavefront shaping
creator: Alba M. Paniagua-Diaz, Adrian Ghita, Tom Vettenburg, Nick Stone, Jacopo Bertolotti
description: Abstract Light scattering limits the penetration depth of non-invasive Raman spectroscopy in biological media. While safe levels of irradiation may be adequate to analyze superficial tissue, scattering of the pump beam reduces the Raman signal to undetectable levels deeper within the tissue.

title: Growth-Temperature Dependence of Conductivity at the LaCrO 3 /SrTiO 3 (001) Interface
creator: A. Al-Tawhid, J. Frick, D.B. Dougherty, D.P. Kumah
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by A. Al-Tawhid, J. Frick, D.B. Dougherty, D.P. Kumah. The effect of growth conditions on the structural and electronic properties of the polar/non-polar LaCrO 3 /SrTiO 3 (LCO/STO) interface has been investigated. The interface is either insulating or metallic depending on growth conditions.

title: AUTOMATIC SHORT ANSWER GRADING AND FEEDBACK USING TEXT MINING METHODS
creator: N. Süzen, A.N. Gorban, J. Levesley, E.M. Mirkes
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by N. Süzen, A.N. Gorban, J. Levesley, E.M. Mirkes. Automatic grading is not a new approach but the need to adapt the latest technology to automatic grading has become very important. As the technology has rapidly became more powerful on scoring exams and essays, especially from the 1990s onwards, partially or wholly automated grading systems using computational methods have evolved and have become a major area of research.

title: Search for vector-boson resonances decaying to a top quark and bottom quark in the lepton plus jets final state in p ​ p pp collisions at s \sqrt{s} = 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for new charged massive gauge bosons, W ′ W^{\prime} , is performed with the ATLAS detector at the LHC. Data were collected in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of s \sqrt{s} = 13 TeV and correspond to an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb -1 36.1\penalty\ \penalty\ \mbox{{{fb}}${}^{-1}$} .

title: Measuring the Boiling Point of the Vacuum of Quantum Electrodynamics
creator: Anthony Hartin, Andreas Ringwald, Natalia Tapia
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Anthony Hartin, Andreas Ringwald, Natalia Tapia. It is a long-standing non-trivial prediction of quantum electrodynamics that its vacuum is unstable in the background of a static, spatially uniform electric field and, in principle, sparks with spontaneous emission of electron-positron pairs.

title: Exploring Sensitivity to NMSSM Signatures with Low Missing Transverse Energy at the LHC
creator: A. Titterton, U. Ellwanger, H.U. Flaecher, S. Moretti, C.H. Shepherd-Themistocleous
description: Abstract We examine scenarios in the Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (NMSSM), where pair-produced squarks and gluinos decay via two cascades, each ending in a stable neutralino as Lightest Supersymmetric Particle (LSP) and a Standard Model (SM)-like Higgs boson, with mass spectra such that the missing transverse energy, E T miss E_{\text{T}}^{\text{miss}} , is very low.

title: An Algorithm for Learning Shape and Appearance Models without Annotations Journal: Medical Image Analysis
creator: John Ashburner, Mikael Brudfors, Kevin Bronik, Yaël Balbastre
description: Abstract This paper presents a framework for automatically learning shape and appearance models for medical (and certain other) images. It is based on the idea that having a more accurate shape and appearance model leads to more accurate image registration, which in turn leads to a more accurate shape and appearance model.

title: Leveraging Medical Sentiment to Understand Patients Health on Social Media
creator: Shweta Yadav, Joy Sain, Amit Sheth, Asif Ekbal, Sriparna Saha, Pushpak Bhattacharyya
description: Abstract The unprecedented growth of Internet users in recent years has resulted in an abundance of unstructured information in the form of social media text. A large percentage of this population is actively engaged in health social networks to share health-related information. In this paper, we address an important and timely topic by analyzing the users’ sentiments and emotions w.r.

title: Towards End-to-End Acoustic Localization using Deep Learning: from Audio Signal to Source Position Coordinates
creator: Juan Manuel Vera-Diaz, Daniel Pizarro, Javier Macias-Guarasa
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Juan Manuel Vera-Diaz, Daniel Pizarro, Javier Macias-Guarasa. This paper presents a novel approach for indoor acoustic source localization using microphone arrays and based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The proposed solution is, to the best of our knowledge, the first published work in which the CNN is designed to directly estimate the three dimensional position of an acoustic source, using the raw audio signal as the input information avoiding the use of hand crafted audio features.

title: DCASE 2018 Challenge - Task 5: Monitoring of domestic activities based on multi-channel acoustics
description: Abstract The DCASE 2018 Challenge consists of five tasks related to automatic classification and detection of sound events and scenes. This paper presents the setup of Task 5 which includes the description of the task, dataset and the baseline system.

title: DataJoint: A Simpler Relational Data Model
creator: Dimitri Yatsenko, Edgar Y. Walker, Andreas S. Tolias
description: Abstract The relational data model offers unrivaled rigor and precision in defining data structure and querying complex data. Yet the use of relational databases in scientific data pipelines is limited due to their perceived unwieldiness. We propose a simplified and conceptually refined relational data model named DataJoint.

title: Concavity of the meson Regge trajectories
creator: Jiao-Kai Chen
description: Abstract It is illustrated by the fitted Regge trajectories for a large majority of mesons that the radial and orbital Regge trajectories for mesons prefer being concave in the ( n r , M 2 ) (n_{r},M^{2}) and ( l , M 2 ) (l,M^{2}) planes, respectively. The concavity of the meson Regge trajectories is model-independent.

title: Game of Orbits: A Gaming Approach to Neptune’s Discovery
creator: Siddharth Bhatnagar, Jayant Murthy
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Bhatnagar, Jayant Murthy. One reason that the planet Neptune will be remembered for, is to do with the fact that it was the first planet whose existence was postulated before being observed. This was based on analysing deviations in Uranus’ orbit. The present study gives a brief account of the history behind the discovery of Neptune, looking at the same, through the conflicting lenses of France and Britain.

title: Parsec: A State Channel for the Internet of Value
creator: Amit Kumar Jaiswal
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Amit Kumar Jaiswal. We propose Parsec, a web-scale State channel for the Internet of Value to exterminate the consensus bottleneck in Blockchain by leveraging a network of state channels which enable to robustly transfer value off-chain. It acts as an infrastructure layer developed on top of Ethereum Blockchain, as a network protocol which allows coherent routing and interlocking channel transfers for trade-off between parties. A web-scale solution for state channels is implemented to enable a layer of value transfer to the internet.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation by Adversarial Learning for Robust Speech Recognition
creator: Pavel Denisov, Ngoc Thang Vu, Marc Ferras Font
description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the use of adversarial learning for unsupervised adaptation to unseen recording conditions, more specifically, single microphone far-field speech. We adapt neural networks based acoustic models trained with close-talk clean speech to the new recording conditions using untranscribed adaptation data. Our experimental results on Italian SPEECON data set show that our proposed method achieves 19.

title: Graphene: Semantically-Linked Propositions in Open Information Extraction
creator: Matthias Cetto, Christina Niklaus, André Freitas, Siegfried Handschuh
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Matthias Cetto, Christina Niklaus, André Freitas, Siegfried Handschuh. We present an Open Information Extraction (IE) approach that uses a two-layered transformation stage consisting of a clausal disembedding layer and a phrasal disembedding layer, together with rhetorical relation identification.

title: RiTUAL-UH at TRAC 2018 Shared Task: Aggression Identification
creator: Niloofar Safi Samghabadi, Deepthi Mave, Sudipta Kar, Thamar Solorio
description: Abstract This paper presents our system for “TRAC 2018 Shared Task on Aggression Identification”. Our best systems for the English dataset use a combination of lexical and semantic features. However, for Hindi data using only lexical features gave us the best results. We obtained weighted F1-measures of 0.5921 for the English Facebook task (ranked 12th), 0.

title: The Serendipity of Electroweak Baryogenesis
creator: Géraldine Servant 1,2
description: Abstract The origin of the matter antimatter asymmetry of the universe remains unexplained in the Standard Model of particle physics. The origin of the flavour structure is another major puzzle of the theory. In this article, we report on recent work attempting to link the two themes through the appealing framework of electroweak baryogenesis.

title: UH-PRHLT at SemEval-2016 Task 3: Combining Lexical and Semantic-based Features for Community Question Answering
creator: Marc Franco-Salvador, Sudipta Kar, Thamar Solorio, Paolo Rosso
description: Abstract In this work we describe the system built for the three English subtasks of the SemEval 2016 Task 3 by the Department of Computer Science of the University of Houston (UH) and the Pattern Recognition and Human Language Technology (PRHLT) research center - Universitat Politècnica de València: UH-PRHLT.

title: Improving Spatiotemporal Self-Supervision by Deep Reinforcement Learning
creator: Uta Büchler, Biagio Brattoli ⋆, Björn Ommer
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Uta Büchler, Biagio Brattoli ⋆, Björn Ommer. Self-supervised learning of convolutional neural networks can harness large amounts of cheap unlabeled data to train powerful feature representations. As surrogate task, we jointly address ordering of visual data in the spatial and temporal domain. The permutations of training samples, which are at the core of self-supervision by ordering, have so far been sampled randomly from a fixed preselected set.

title: Leveraging Motion Priors in Videos for Improving Human Segmentation
creator: Yu-Ting Chen, Wen-Yen Chang, Hai-Lun Lu, Tingfan Wu, Min Sun
description: Abstract Despite many advances in deep-learning based semantic segmentation, performance drop due to distribution mismatch is often encountered in the real world. Recently, a few domain adaptation and active learning approaches have been proposed to mitigate the performance drop. However, very little attention has been made toward leveraging information in videos which are naturally captured in most camera systems.

title: Search for a \PWpr boson decaying to a \Pgt \Pgt lepton and a neutrino in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
description: Abstract A search for a new high-mass resonance decaying to a \Pgt \Pgt lepton and a neutrino is reported. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV , corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv . The search utilizes hadronically decaying \Pgt \Pgt leptons.

title: A Zero-Shot Framework for Sketch based Image Retrieval
creator: Sasi Kiran Yelamarthi 1, Shiva Krishna Reddy 1, Ashish Mishra, Anurag Mittal
description: Abstract Sketch-based image retrieval (SBIR) is the task of retrieving images from a natural image database that correspond to a given hand-drawn sketch. Ideally, an SBIR model should learn to associate components in the sketch (say, feet, tail, etc.) with the corresponding components in the image having similar shape characteristics.

title: Extreme quasars at high redshift
creator: M. L. Martínez-Aldama, A. del Olmo, P. Marziani, J. W. Sulentic, C.A. Negrete, D. Dultzin, M. D’Onofrio, J. Perea
description: Abstract Context. Quasars radiating at extreme Eddington ratios (hereafter xA quasars) are likely a prime mover of galactic evolution and have been hailed as potential distance indicators. Their properties are still scarcely known. Aims. We test the effectiveness of the selection criteria defined on the “4D Eigenvector 1” (4DE1) for identifying xA sources.

title: A study on spline quasi–interpolation based quadrature rules for the isogeometric Galerkin BEM
creator: Antonella Falini, Tadej Kanduč
description: Abstract Two recently introduced quadrature schemes for weakly singular integrals [ 1 ] are investigated in the context of boundary integral equations arising in the isogeometric formulation of Galerkin Boundary Element Method (BEM). In the first scheme, the regular part of the integrand is approximated by a suitable quasi–interpolation spline.

title: Optimal exponentials of thickness in Korn’s inequalities for parabolic and elliptic shells
creator: Peng-Fei YAO
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Peng-Fei YAO. This work is supported by the National Science Foundation of China, grants no. 61573342, and Key Research Program of Frontier Sciences, CAS, no. Abstract We establish Korn’s interpolation inequalities and the rigidity results of the strain tensor of the middle surface for the parabolic and elliptic shells and show that the best constant in Korn’s inequalities scales like h^{3/2} for the parabolic shell and h for the elliptic shell, removing the main assumption that the middle surface of the shell is given

title: Ground state representations of some non-rational conformal nets
creator: Yoh Tanimoto
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Yoh Tanimoto. We construct families of ground state representations of the U ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathrm{U}(1) -current net and of the Virasoro nets Vir c {\rm Vir}_{c} with central charge c ≥ 1 c\geq 1 . We show that these representations are not covariant with respect to the original dilations, and those on the U ⁡ ( 1 ) {\rm U(1)} -current net are not solitonic.

title: Text Normalization using Memory Augmented Neural Networks Journal: Speech Communication
creator: Subhojeet Pramanik, Aman Hussain
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Subhojeet Pramanik, Aman Hussain. We perform text normalization, i.e. the transformation of words from the written to the spoken form, using a memory augmented neural network. With the addition of dynamic memory access and storage mechanism, we present a neural architecture that will serve as a language-agnostic text normalization system while avoiding the kind of unacceptable errors made by the LSTM-based recurrent neural networks. By successfully reducing the frequency of such mistakes, we show that this novel architecture is indeed a better alternative.

title: Pseudorapidity dependence of particle production and elliptic flow in asymmetric nuclear collisions of p p + + Al, p p + + Au, d d + + Au, and 3 He + + Au at s N ​ N = 200 \sqrt{s_{{}_{NN}}}=200 GeV
creator: A. Adare, C. Aidala, N.N. Ajitanand, Y. Akiba, M. Alfred, V. Andrieux, K. Aoki, N. Apadula, H. Asano, C. Ayuso, B. Azmoun, V. Babintsev, M. Bai, N.S. Bandara, B. Bannier, K.N. Barish, S. Bathe, A. Bazilevsky, M. Beaumier, S. Beckman, R. Belmont, A. Berdnikov, Y. Berdnikov, D.S. Blau, M. Boer, J.S. B
description: Abstract Asymmetric nuclear collisions of p p + + Al, p p + + Au, d d + + Au, and 3 He + + Au at s N ​ N = 200 \sqrt{s_{{}_{NN}}}=200 GeV provide an excellent laboratory for understanding particle production, as well as exploring interactions among these particles after their initial creation in the collision.

title: Freezing-in dark matter through a heavy invisible Z ′ Z^{\prime} Preprint: LPT–Orsay 18-14
creator: Gautam Bhattacharyya a, Maíra Dutra b, Yann Mambrini b, Mathias Pierre b
description: Abstract We demonstrate that in a class of the U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} extension of the Standard Model (SM), under which all the Standard Model matter fields are uncharged and the additional neutral gauge boson Z ′ Z^{\prime} couples to a set of heavy nonstandard fermions, dark matter (DM) production mediated by Z ′ Z^{\prime} can proceed

title: Multi-vehicle Flocking Control with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Method
creator: Yang Lyu, Quan Pan, Jinwen Hu, Chunhui Zhao, Shuai Liu
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Yang Lyu, Quan Pan, Jinwen Hu, Chunhui Zhao, Shuai Liu. Flocking control has been studied extensively along with the wide application of multi-vehicle systems. In this paper the Multi-vehicles System (MVS) flocking control with collision avoidance and communication preserving is considered based on the deep reinforcement learning framework. Specifically the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) with centralized training and distributed execution process is implemented to obtain the flocking control policy.

title: S. Acharya
description: Abstract Comprehensive results on the production of unidentified charged particles, π ± \pi^{\pm} , K ± \mathrm{K}^{\pm} , K S 0 {\rm K}^{0}_{\rm S} , K*(892) 0 , p \rm p , p ¯ \rm\overline{p} , ϕ \phi (1020), Λ \Lambda , Λ ¯ \overline{\Lambda} , Ξ − \Xi^{-} , Ξ ¯ + \overline{\Xi}^{+} , Ω − \Omega^{-} and Ω

title: Weak ergodic theorem for Markov chains without invariant countably additive measures
creator: Alexander Zhdanok
description: Abstract In this paper, we study Markov chains (MC) on topological spaces within the framework of the operator approach. We extend the Markov operator from the space of countably additive measures to the space of finitely additive measures. Cesaro means for a Markov sequence of measures and their asymptotic behavior in the weak topology are considered.

title: Critical Phenomena of Charged de Sitter Black Holes in Cavities
creator: Fil Simovic 1,2 , Robert B. Mann 2
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Fil Simovic 1,2 , Robert B. Mann 2. We examine the thermodynamic behaviour of four-dimensional charged and uncharged de Sitter black holes enclosed in an isothermal cavity, in the extended phase space where the cosmological constant is treated as a thermodynamic pressure.

title: MONET: Multiview Semi-supervised Keypoint Detection via Epipolar Divergence
creator: Yuan Yao, Yasamin Jafarian, Hyun Soo Park
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Yuan Yao, Yasamin Jafarian, Hyun Soo Park. This paper presents MONET—an end-to-end semi-supervised learning framework for a keypoint detector using multiview image streams. In particular, we consider general subjects such as non-human species where attaining a large scale annotated dataset is challenging. While multiview geometry can be used to self-supervise the unlabeled data, integrating the geometry into learning a keypoint detector is challenging due to representation mismatch.

title: A Survey of Domain Adaptation for Neural Machine Translation
creator: Chenhui Chu, Rui Wang
description: Abstract Neural machine translation (NMT) is a deep learning based approach for machine translation, which yields the state-of-the-art translation performance in scenarios where large-scale parallel corpora are available. Although the high-quality and domain-specific translation is crucial in the real world, domain-specific corpora are usually scarce or nonexistent, and thus vanilla NMT performs poorly in such scenarios.

title: On the Security Analysis of a Cooperative Incremental Relaying Protocol in the Presence of an Active Eavesdropper
creator: Saeed Vahidian, Sajad Hatamnia, and Benoit Champagne,
description: Abstract Physical layer security offers an efficient means to decrease the risk of confidential information leakage through wiretap links. In this paper, we address the physical-layer security in a cooperative wireless subnetwork that includes a source-destination pair and multiple relays, exchanging information in the presence of a malevolent eavesdropper.

title: High-Order Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations of a Spinning Golf Ball Journal: Sports Engineering
creator: Jacob Crabill, Freddie Witherden, Antony Jameson
description: Abstract This paper presents the first high-order computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of static and spinning golf balls at realistic flow conditions. The present results are shown to capture the complex fluid dynamics inside the dimples which lead to drag reduction versus a smooth sphere, and compare well to previous experimental and computational studies.

title: Direct optimisation of the discovery significance when training neural networks to search for new physics in particle colliders
creator: and Dirk Krücker
description: Abstract We introduce two new loss functions designed to directly optimise the statistical significance of the expected number of signal events when training neural networks to classify events as signal or background in the scenario of a search for new physics at a particle collider.

title: Introduction to Fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces
creator: Mohammed SRATI 1 Elhoussine AZROUL 2 Abdelmoujib BENKIRANE 3
description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 46E30, 46E35, 35R11, 35J60. Abstract In this paper, we define the fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces, and we prove some important results of these spaces. The main result is to show the continuous and compact embedding for these spaces.

title: Power Corrections for N-Jettiness Subtractions at 𝒪 ⁡ ( 𝜶 𝒔 ) {\cal O}(\alpha_{s})\!\! Preprint: MIT-CTP 5007 DESY 18-120
creator: Markus A. Ebert, Ian Moult, Iain W. Stewart, Frank J. Tackmann, Gherardo Vita, and Hua Xing Zhu
description: Abstract We continue the study of power corrections for N N -jettiness subtractions by analytically computing the complete next-to-leading power corrections at 𝒪 ⁡ ( α s ) {\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_{s}) for color-singlet production. This includes all nonlogarithmic terms and all partonic channels for Drell-Yan and gluon-fusion Higgs production.

title: Fast Artificial Immune Systems
creator: Dogan Corus, Pietro S. Oliveto, Donya Yazdani
description: Abstract Various studies have shown that characteristic Artificial Immune System (AIS) operators such as hypermutations and ageing can be very efficient at escaping local optima of multimodal optimisation problems. However, this efficiency comes at the expense of considerably slower runtimes during the exploitation phase compared to standard evolutionary algorithms.

title: Gradient resummation for nonlinear chiral transport: an insight from holography
creator: Yanyan Bu, Tuna Demircik, Michael Lublinsky
description: Abstract Nonlinear transport phenomena induced by chiral anomaly are explored within a 4D field theory defined holographically as U ​ ( 1 ) V × U ​ ( 1 ) A U(1)_{V}\times U(1)_{A} Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory in Schwarzschild- A ​ d ​ S 5 AdS_{5} .

title: Mahler’s work on the geometry of numbers Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 11H06, 11H16, 11H60 Thanks: Keywords and Phrases: star bodies, critical lattices, compound convex bodies, successive minima, transference principles Thanks: August 9, 2026
creator: Jan-Hendrik Evertse
description: Abstract Mahler has written many papers on the geometry of numbers. Arguably, his most influential achievements in this area are his compactness theorem for lattices, his work on star bodies and their critical lattices, and his estimates for the successive minima of reciprocal convex bodies and compound convex bodies.

title: Amplification of quadratic Hamiltonians
creator: Christian Arenz, Denys I. Bondar, Daniel Burgarth, Cecilia Cormick, Herschel Rabitz
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Christian Arenz, Denys I. Bondar, Daniel Burgarth, Cecilia Cormick, Herschel Rabitz. Speeding up the dynamics of a quantum system is of paramount importance for quantum technologies. However, in finite dimensions and without full knowledge of the details of the system, it is easily shown to be impossible . In contrast we show that continuous variable systems described by a certain class of quadratic Hamiltonians can be sped up without such detailed knowledge. We call the resultant procedure Hamiltonian amplification (HA).

title: Mahler’s work on Diophantine equations and subsequent developments Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 11D25, 11D45, 11D57, 11D59, 11D61, 11J61, 11J68 Thanks: Keywords and Phrases: Thue-Mahler equations, Unit equations, Elliptic curves, Diophantine approximation, decomposable form equat
creator: Jan-Hendrik Evertse, Kálmán Győry, Cameron L. Stewart
description: Abstract The main body of Mahler’s work on Diophantine equations consists of his 1933 papers [ 54 , 55 , 56 ] , in which he proved a generalization of the Thue-Siegel Theorem on the approximation of algebraic numbers by rationals, involving P -adic absolute values, and applied this to get finiteness results for the number of solutions for what

title: Search for Higgs boson pair production in the γ ​ γ ​ \bbbar \gamma\gamma\bbbar final state in \Pp ​ \Pp \Pp\Pp collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by . A search is presented for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons, where one decays into two photons and the other one into a bottom quark-antiquark pair. The analysis is performed using proton-proton collision data at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV recorded in 2016 by the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv . The results are in agreement with standard model (SM) predictions.

title: Pattern Search Multidimensional Scaling
creator: Georgios Paraskevopoulos, Efthymios Tzinis *, Emmanuel-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Alexandros Potamianos
description: Abstract We present a novel view of nonlinear manifold learning using derivative-free optimization techniques. Specifically, we propose an extension of the classical multi-dimensional scaling (MDS) method, where instead of performing gradient descent, we sample and evaluate possible “moves” in a sphere of fixed radius for each point in the embedded space.

title: Artificial Immune Systems Can Find Arbitrarily Good Approximations for the NP-Hard Number Partitioning Problem Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
creator: Dogan Corus, Pietro S. Oliveto, Donya Yazdani
description: Abstract Typical artificial immune system (AIS) operators such as hypermutations with mutation potential and ageing allow to efficiently overcome local optima from which evolutionary algorithms (EAs) struggle to escape. Such behaviour has been shown for artificial example functions constructed especially to show difficulties that EAs may encounter during the optimisation process.

title: Assessing Perturbativity and Vacuum Stability in High-Scale Leptogenesis Preprint: IPPP/18/40 FERMILAB-PUB-18-222-T UCI-TR-2018-05
creator: Seyda Ipek, Alexis D. Plascencia, and Jessica Turner
description: Abstract We consider the requirements that all coupling constants remain perturbative and the electroweak vacuum metastable up to the Planck scale in high-scale thermal leptogenesis, in the context of a type-I seesaw mechanism. We find a large region of the model parameter space that satisfies these conditions in combination with producing the baryon asymmetry of the Universe.

title: Signals on the power spectra of a cosmology modeled with Chebyshev polynomials
creator: Freddy Cueva Solano
description: Abstract We present an interacting model with a phenomenological interaction, Q ¯ \bar{Q} , between a cold dark matter (DM) fluid and a dark energy (DE) fluid, which takes a time-varying equation of state (EoS) parameter, ω DE \mathrm{\omega_{DE}} . Here, both Q ¯ \bar{Q} and ω DE \mathrm{\omega_{DE}} are modeled in terms of the Chebyschev polynomials.

title: Search for dark matter in events with a hadronically decaying vector boson and missing transverse momentum in p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for dark matter (DM) particles produced in association with a hadronically decaying vector boson is performed using p ​ p pp collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb -1 , recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider.

title: The Complexity of Bisimulation and Simulation on Finite Systems
creator: Moses Ganardi, Stefan Göller, Markus Lohrey
description: Abstract . In this paper the computational complexity of the (bi)simulation problem over restricted graph classes is studied. For trees given as pointer structures or terms the (bi)simulation problem is complete for logarithmic space or 𝖭𝖢 1 {\sf NC}^{1} , respectively. This solves an open problem from Balcázar, Gabarró, and Sántha.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Model Order Reduction in Seismic Full-Waveform Inversion
creator: Alan Richardson (Ausar Geophysical)
description: Abstract I train a Generative Adversarial Network to produce realistic seismic wave speed models. I integrate the generator network into seismic Full-Waveform Inversion to reduce the number of model parameters and restrict the inverted models to only those that are plausible.

title: Bounds for polynomials on algebraic numbers and application to curve topology
creator: Daouda Niang Diatta, Sény Diatta, Fabrice Rouillier, Marie-Françoise Roy, Michael Sagraloff
description: Abstract Let P ∈ ℤ ⁡ [ X , Y ] P\in\mathbb{Z}[X,Y] be a given square-free polynomial of total degree d d with integer coefficients of bitsize less than τ \tau , and let V ℝ ​ ( P ) := { ( x , y ) ∈ ℝ 2 , P ⁡ ( x , y ) = 0

title: Accelerating Incremental Gradient Optimization with Curvature Information
creator: Hoi-To Wai, Wei Shi, César A. Uribe, Angelia Nedić, Anna Scaglione In memory of Dr. Wei Shi, a respected friend and talented scholar.
description: Abstract This paper studies an acceleration technique for incremental aggregated gradient ( IAG ) method through the use of curvature information for solving strongly convex finite sum optimization problems. These optimization problems of interest arise in large-scale learning applications. Our technique utilizes a curvature-aided gradient tracking step to produce accurate gradient estimates incrementally using Hessian information.

title: Learning and Generalizing Motion Primitives from Driving Data for Path-Tracking Applications
creator: Boyang Wang, Zirui Li, Jianwei Gong, Yidi Liu, Huiyan Chen, Chao Lu
description: Abstract Considering the driving habits which are learned from the naturalistic driving data in the path-tracking system can significantly improve the acceptance of intelligent vehicles. Therefore, the goal of this paper is to generate the prediction results of lateral commands with confidence regions according to the reference based on the learned motion primitives.

title: TernausNetV2: Fully Convolutional Network for Instance Segmentation
creator: Vladimir I. Iglovikov, Selim S. Seferbekov, Alexander V. Buslaev, Alexey A. Shvets
description: Abstract The most common approaches to instance segmentation are complex and use two-stage networks with object proposals, conditional random-fields, template matching or recurrent neural networks. In this work we present TernausNetV2 - a fully convolutional network that allows extracting objects from a high-resolution satellite imagery on an instance level.

title: Angular analysis of the decay \PBp → \PKp ​ \Pgmp ​ \Pgmm \PBp\to\PKp\Pgmp\Pgmm in proton-proton collisions at s = 8 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=8\TeV
description: Abstract The angular distribution of the flavor-changing neutral current decay \PBp → \PKp ​ \Pgmp ​ \Pgmm \PBp\to\PKp\Pgmp\Pgmm is studied in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 8 \TeV . The analysis is based on data collected with the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 20.5 \fbinv .

title: Barcodes for closed one form - an alternative to Novikov theory
creator: Dan Burghelea
description: Abstract We extend the configurations δ r \delta_{r} and γ r \gamma_{r} , discussed in [ 1 ] and [ 4 ] , equivalently the closed, open and closed-open bar codes from real- or angle-valued maps, to topological closed one forms on compact ANRs.

title: CepGen – A generic central exclusive processes event generator for hadron-hadron collisions
creator: Laurent Forthomme
description: Abstract We present an event generator for the simulation of central exclusive processes in hadron-hadron reactions. Among others, it implements the two-photon production of lepton pairs previously introduced in LPAIR. As a proof of principle, we show that the two approaches are numerically consistent.

title: CrowdTruth 2.0: Quality Metrics for Crowdsourcing with Disagreement
creator: Anca Dumitrache, Oana Inel, Benjamin Timmermans, Chris Welty
description: Abstract Typically crowdsourcing-based approaches to gather annotated data use inter-annotator agreement as a measure of quality. However, in many domains, there is ambiguity in the data, as well as a multitude of perspectives of the information examples. In this paper, we present ongoing work into the CrowdTruth metrics, that capture and interpret inter-annotator disagreement in crowdsourcing.

title: Transverse link invariants from the deformations of Khovanov 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 3 \mathfrak{sl}_{3} -homology
creator: Carlo Collari
description: Abstract . In this paper we will make use of the Mackaay-Vaz approach to the universal 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 3 \mathfrak{sl}_{3} -homology to define a family of cycles (called β 3 \beta_{3} -invariants) which are transverse braid invariants. This family includes Wu’s ψ 3 \psi_{3} -invariant.

title: Unitary Extension Principle for Nonuniform Wavelet Frames in L 2 ​ ( ℝ ) L^{2}(\mathbb{R})
creator: Hari Krishan Malhotra, Lalit Kumar Vashisht
description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Hari Krishan Malhotra, Lalit Kumar Vashisht. We study the construction of nonuniform tight wavelet frames for the Lebesgue space L 2 ​ ( ℝ ) L^{2}(\mathbb{R}) , where the related translation set is not necessary a group. The main purpose of this paper is to prove the unitary extension principle (UEP) and the oblique extension principle (OEP) for construction of multi-generated nonuniform tight wavelet frames for L 2 ​ ( ℝ ) L^{2}(\mathbb{R}) . Some examples are also given to illustrate the results.

title: Elasticizing Linux via Joint Disaggregation of Memory and Computation
creator: Ehab Ababneh, Zaid Al-Ali, Sangtae Ha, Richard Han, Eric Keller
description: Abstract Abstract In this paper, we propose a set of operating system primitives which provides a scaling abstraction to cloud applications in which they can transparently be enabled to support scaled execution across multiple physical nodes as resource needs go beyond that available on a single machine.

title: A Framework for Aggregating Private and Public Web Archives
