title: Depthwise Hyperparameter Transfer in Residual Networks: Dynamics and Scaling Limit
creator: Blake Bordelon, Lorenzo Noci, Mufan (Bill) Li, Boris Hanin & Cengiz Pehlevan
description: Abstract The cost of hyperparameter tuning in deep learning has been rising with model sizes, prompting practitioners to find new tuning methods using a proxy of smaller networks. One such proposal uses μ \mu P parameterized networks, where the optimal hyperparameters for small width networks transfer to networks with arbitrarily large width.

title: A Direct k k -Way Hypergraph Partitioning Algorithm for Optimizing the Steiner Tree Metric
creator: Tobias Heuer
description: Abstract Minimizing wire-lengths is one of the most important objectives in circuit design. The process involves initially placing the logical units (cells) of a circuit onto a physical layout, and subsequently routing the wires to connect the cells. Hypergraph partitioning (HGP) has been long used as a placement strategy in this process.

title: Effects of bulk viscosity, heat capacity ratio and Prandtl number on the dispersion relationship of the compressible Navier-Stokes equation
creator: Swagata Bhaumik 3, Sawant Omkar Deepak 1
description: Abstract Here, variation of the dispersion characteristics of 3D linearized compressible Navier-Stokes equation (NSE) with respect to bulk viscosity ratio ( κ / μ \kappa/\mu ), specific heat ratio γ \gamma and Prandtl number P ​ r Pr is presented. The 3D compressible NSE supports five type of waves, two vortical, one entropic and two acoustic modes.

title: A stable-compact method for qualitative properties of semilinear elliptic equations
creator: Henri Berestycki, Cole Graham
description: Abstract . We study the uniqueness of reaction-diffusion steady states in general domains with Dirichlet boundary data. Here we consider “positive” (monostable) reactions. We describe geometric conditions on the domain that ensure uniqueness and we provide complementary examples of nonuniqueness. Along the way, we formulate a number of open problems and conjectures.

title: Cubical Approximation for Directed Topology II
creator: Sanjeevi Krishnan
description: Abstract . The paper establishes an equivalence between localizations of (diagrams of) cubical sets and (diagrams of) directed topological spaces by those maps defining (natural) cubical homotopy equivalences after application of the directed singular functor and a directed analogue of fibrant replacement. This equivalence both lifts and extends an equivalence between classical homotopy categories of cubical sets and topological spaces.

title: Uncertainty principles associated with the short time quaternion coupled fractional Fourier transform
creator: Bivek Gupta, Amit K. Verma, Ravi P. Agarwal
description: Abstract In this paper, we extend the coupled fractional Fourier transform of a complex valued functions to that of the quaternion valued functions on ℝ 4 \mathbb{R}^{4} and call it the quaternion coupled fractional Fourier transform (QCFrFT). We obtain the sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality for QCFrFT and obtain the associated Rènyi uncertainty principle.

title: Framework and Model Analysis on Bengali Document Layout Analysis Dataset: BaDLAD Thanks: DL Sprint 2.0 [ 2 ] has provided this opportunity to extend our knowledge and research on bengali document analysis
creator: Kazi Reyazul Hasan 1 , Mubasshira Musarrat 2 , Sadif Ahmed 3 , and Shahriar Raj 4
description: Abstract This study focuses on understanding Bengali Document Layouts using advanced computer programs: Detectron2, YOLOv8, and SAM. We looked at lots of different Bengali documents in our study. Detectron2 is great at finding and separating different parts of documents, like textboxes and paragraphs. YOLOv8 is good at figuring out different tables and pictures.

title: UAV-assisted Semantic Communication with Hybrid Action Reinforcement Learning
creator: Peiyuan Si 1 , Jun Zhao 1 , Kwok-Yan Lam 1 , Qing Yang 2
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Peiyuan Si 1 , Jun Zhao 1 , Kwok-Yan Lam 1 , Qing Yang 2. In this paper, we aim to explore the use of uplink semantic communications with the assistance of UAV in order to improve data collection effiicency for metaverse users in remote areas.

title: MV-DeepSDF: Implicit Modeling with Multi-Sweep Point Clouds for 3D Vehicle Reconstruction in Autonomous Driving
creator: Yibo Liu, Kelly Zhu, Guile Wu, Yuan Ren, Bingbing Liu, Yang Liu, Jinjun Shan
description: Abstract Reconstructing 3D vehicles from noisy and sparse partial point clouds is of great significance to autonomous driving. Most existing 3D reconstruction methods cannot be directly applied to this problem because they are elaborately designed to deal with dense inputs with trivial noise.

title: Energy Efficient Foot-Shape Design for Bipedal Walkers on Granular Terrain Address all correspondence to J. Yi.
creator: Xunjie Chen, Jingang Yi, Hao Wang
description: Abstract It is important to understand how bipedal walkers balance and walk effectively on granular materials, such as sand and loose dirt, etc. This paper first presents a computational approach to obtain the motion and energy analysis of bipedal walkers on granular terrains and then discusses an optimization method for the robot foot-shape contour design for energy efficiently walking.

title: Local minima in quantum systems
creator: Chi-Fang Anthony Chen, Hsin-Yuan Huang, John Preskill, Leo Zhou
description: Abstract Finding ground states of quantum many-body systems is known to be hard for both classical and quantum computers. As a result, when Nature cools a quantum system in a low-temperature thermal bath, the ground state cannot always be found efficiently. Instead, Nature finds a local minimum of the energy.

title: Merging automatic differentiation and the adjoint method for photonic inverse design
creator: Alexander Luce, Rasoul Alaee, Fabian Knorr, Florian Marquardt
description: Abstract Optimizing shapes and topology of physical devices is crucial for both scientific and technological advancements, given its wide-ranging implications across numerous industries and research areas. Innovations in shape and topology optimization have been seen across a wide range of fields, notably structural mechanics, fluid mechanics, and photonics.

title: General Lipschitz: Certified Robustness Against Resolvable Semantic Transformations via Transformation-Dependent Randomized Smoothing
creator: Dmitrii Korzh, Mikhail Pautov, Olga Tsymboi, Ivan Oseledets
description: Abstract Randomized smoothing is the state-of-the-art approach to constructing image classifiers that are provably robust against additive adversarial perturbations of bounded magnitude. However, it is more complicated to compute reasonable certificates against semantic transformations (e.g., image blurring, translation, gamma correction) and their compositions.

title: ELIP: Efficient Language-Image Pre-training with Fewer Vision Tokens
creator: Yangyang Guo, Haoyu Zhang, Yongkang Wong, Liqiang Nie, Mohan Kankanhalli
description: Abstract Learning a versatile language-image model is computationally prohibitive under a limited computing budget. This paper delves into the efficient language-image pre-training , an area that has received relatively little attention despite its importance in reducing computational cost and footprint.

title: Modular quantum signal processing in many variables
creator: Zane M. Rossi, Jack L. Ceroni, Isaac L. Chuang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zane M. Rossi, Jack L. Ceroni, Isaac L. Chuang. Despite significant advances in quantum algorithms, quantum programs in practice are often expressed at the circuit level, forgoing helpful structural abstractions common to their classical counterparts. Consequently, as many quantum algorithms have been unified with the advent of quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT), an opportunity has appeared to cast these algorithms as modules that can be combined to constitute complex programs.

title: Kaniadakis entropy-based characterization of IceCube PeV neutrino signals
creator: M. Blasone, G. Lambiase, G. G. Luciano
description: Abstract Kaniadakis κ \kappa -thermostatistics is by now recognized as an effective paradigm to describe relativistic complex systems obeying power-law tailed distributions, as opposed to the classical (exponential-type) decay. It is founded on a non-extensive one-parameter generalization of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, which, in the cosmological framework, gives rise to modified Friedmann equations on the basis of the gravity-thermodynamic conjecture.

title: Erratum to the paper: Asymptotic Invariants of Base Loci
creator: Lawrence Ein, Robert Lazarsfeld, Mircea Mustaţă, Michael Nakamaye, Mihnea Popa
description: Abstract . This note points out a gap in the proof of one of the technical results in the paper Asymptotic Invariants of Base Loci , that appeared in Ann. Inst. Fourier (Grenoble) 56 (2006), 1701–1734. We provide a correct proof of this result. 1.

title: From quantum electrodynamics to a geometric gauge theory of classical electromagnetism
creator: Adam Marsh
description: Abstract A relativistic version of the correspondence principle, a limit in which classical electrodynamics may be derived from QED, has never been clear, especially when including gravitational mass. Here we introduce a novel classical field theory formulation of electromagnetism, and then show that it approximates QED in the limit of a quantum state which corresponds to a classical charged continua.

title: Supervised Learning Models for Early Detection of Albuminuria Risk in Type-2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients Thanks: * Corresponding author
creator: 1 st Arief Purnama Muharram *, 2 nd Dicky Levenus Tahapary *, 3 rd Yeni Dwi Lestari, 4 th Randy Sarayar, 5 th Valerie Josephine Dirjayanto
description: Abstract Diabetes, especially T2DM, continues to be a significant health problem. One of the major concerns associated with diabetes is the development of its complications. Diabetic nephropathy, one of the chronic complication of diabetes, adversely affects the kidneys, leading to kidney damage.

title: Perverse coherent extensions on Calabi-Yau threefolds and representations of cohomological Hall algebras
creator: Dylan Butson, Miroslav Rapčák
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dylan Butson, Miroslav Rapčák. For Y → X Y\to X a toric Calabi-Yau threefold resolution and M ∈ D b ​ Coh ​ ( Y ) T M\in{\textup{D}}^{b}\textup{Coh}(Y)^{T} satisfying some hypotheses, we define a stack 𝔐 ⁡ ( Y , M ) \mathfrak{M}(Y,M) parameterizing perverse coherent extensions of M M , iterated extensions of M M and the compactly supported perverse coherent sheaves of Bridgeland.

title: Folding QQ-relations and transfer matrix eigenvalues: towards a unified approach to Bethe ansatz for super spin chains
creator: Zengo Tsuboi
description: Abstract Extending the method proposed in [ T11 ] , we derive QQ-relations (functional relations among Baxter Q-functions) and T-functions (eigenvalues of transfer matrices) for fusion vertex models associated with the twisted quantum affine superalgebras U q ​ ( g ​ l ​ ( 2 ​ r + 1 | 2 ​ s ) ( 2 ) ) U_{q}(gl(2r+1|2s)^{(2)}) ,

title: Efficient Training of One Class Classification - SVMs
creator: Isaac A. Yowetu, Nana K. Frempong
description: Abstract This study examines the use of a highly effective training method to conduct one-class classification. The existence of both positive and negative examples in the training data is necessary to develop an effective classifier in common binary classification scenarios. Unfortunately, this criteria is not met in many domains. Here, there is just one class of examples.

title: Implicit Gaussian process representation of vector fields over arbitrary latent manifolds
creator: Robert L. Peach*, Matteo Vinao-Carl*, Nir Grossman, Michael David, Emma Mallas, David Sharp, Paresh A. Malhotra, Pierre Vandergheynst, Adam Gosztolai
description: Abstract Gaussian processes (GPs) are popular nonparametric statistical models for learning unknown functions and quantifying the spatiotemporal uncertainty in data. Recent works have extended GPs to model scalar and vector quantities distributed over non-Euclidean domains, including smooth manifolds appearing in numerous fields such as computer vision, dynamical systems, and neuroscience.

title: Memory in Plain Sight Surveying the Uncanny Resemblances of Associative Memory and Diffusion Models
creator: Benjamin Hoover, Hendrik Strobelt, Dmitry Krotov, Judy Hoffman, Zsolt Kira, Duen Horng Chau
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Hoover, Hendrik Strobelt, Dmitry Krotov, Judy Hoffman, Zsolt Kira, Duen Horng Chau. The generative process of Diffusion Models (DMs) has recently set state-of-the-art on many AI generation benchmarks. Though the generative process is traditionally understood as an “iterative denoiser”, there is no universally accepted language to describe it.

title: Discovering Environments with XRM
creator: Mohammad Pezeshki, Diane Bouchacourt, Mark Ibrahim, Nicolas Ballas, Pascal Vincent, David Lopez-Paz
description: Abstract Environment annotations are essential for the success of many out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization methods. Unfortunately, these are costly to obtain and often limited by human annotators’ biases. To achieve robust generalization, it is essential to develop algorithms for automatic environment discovery within datasets. Current proposals, which divide examples based on their training error, suffer from one fundamental problem.

title: An Object Condensation Pipeline for Charged Particle Tracking at the High Luminosity LHC
creator: \firstname Kilian \lastname Lieret \fnsep, \firstname Gage \lastname DeZoort \fnsep
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by \firstname Kilian \lastname Lieret \fnsep, \firstname Gage \lastname DeZoort \fnsep. Recent work has demonstrated that graph neural networks (GNNs) trained for charged particle tracking can match the performance of traditional algorithms while improving scalability to prepare for the High Luminosity LHC experiment. Most approaches are based on the edge classification (EC) paradigm, wherein tracker hits are connected by edges, and a GNN is trained to prune edges, resulting in a collection of connected components representing tracks.

title: Neural scaling laws for phenotypic drug discovery
creator: Drew Linsley, John Griffin, Jason Parker Brown, Adam N Roose, Michael Frank, Peter Linsley, Steven Finkbeiner, Jeremy Linsley {drewlinsley, jeremylinsley}@operant.bio
description: Abstract Recent breakthroughs by deep neural networks (DNNs) in natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision have been driven by a scale-up of models and data rather than the discovery of novel computing paradigms. Here, we investigate if scale can have a similar impact for models designed to aid small molecule drug discovery.

title: A note on the Hamiltonian structure of transgression forms
creator: Pablo Pais, Patricio Salgado-Rebolledo, Aldo Vera
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pablo Pais, Patricio Salgado-Rebolledo, Aldo Vera. By incorporating two gauge connections, transgression forms provide a generalization of Chern-Simons actions that are genuinely gauge-invariant on bounded manifolds. In this work, we show that, when defined on a manifold with a boundary, the Hamiltonian formulation of a transgression field theory can be consistently carried out without the need to implement regularizing boundary terms at the level of first-class constraints.

title: Encountered-Type Haptic Display via Tracking Calibrated Robot
creator: Chenxi Xiao, Yuan Tian
description: Abstract In the past decades, a variety of haptic devices have been developed to facilitate high-fidelity human-computer interaction (HCI) in virtual reality (VR). In particular, passive haptic feedback can create a compelling sensation based on real objects spatially overlapping with their virtual counterparts. However, these approaches require pre-deployment efforts, hindering their democratizing use in practice.

title: How Many Words Does ChatGPT Know? The Answer is ChatWords
creator: Gonzalo Martínez, Javier Conde, Pedro Reviriego, Elena Merino-Gómez, José Alberto Hernández, Fabrizio Lombardi
description: Abstract The introduction of ChatGPT has put Artificial Intelligence (AI) Natural Language Processing (NLP) in the spotlight. ChatGPT adoption has been exponential with millions of users experimenting with it in a myriad of tasks and application domains with impressive results. However, ChatGPT has limitations and suffers hallucinations, for example producing answers that look plausible but they are completely wrong.

title: Secondary Whistler and Ion-cyclotron Instabilities driven by Mirror Modes in Galaxy Clusters
creator: Francisco Ley, Ellen G. Zweibel, Drake Miller, Mario Riquelme
description: Abstract Electron cyclotron waves (whistlers), are commonly observed in plasmas near Earth and the solar wind. In the presence of nonlinear mirror modes, bursts of whistlers, usually called lion roars, have been observed within low magnetic field regions associated to these modes.

title: Deciphering Pre-solar-storm Features Of September-2017 Storm From Global And Local Dynamics
creator: Breno Raphaldini, Mausumi Dikpati, Aimee A. Norton, Andre S. W. Teruya, Scott W. McIntosh, Christopher B. Prior, David MacTaggart
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Breno Raphaldini, Mausumi Dikpati, Aimee A. Norton, Andre S. W. Teruya, Scott W. McIntosh, Christopher B. Prior, David MacTaggart. We investigate whether global toroid patterns and the local magnetic field topology of solar active region AR12673 together can hindcast occurrence of the biggest X-flare of solar cycle (SC)-24.

title: Surface plasmon-polaritons in graphene, embedded into medium with gain and losses
creator: O. A. Zhernovnykova, O. V. Popova, G. V. Deynychenko, T. I. Deynichenko, Yu. V. Bludov
description: Abstract The paper deals with the theoretical consideration of surface plasmon-polaritons in the graphene monolayer, embedded into dielectric with spatially separated gain and losses. It is demonstrated, that presence of gain and losses in the system leads to the formation of additional mode of graphene surface plasmon-polaritons, which does not have its counterpart in the conservative system.

title: Extensible Consent Management Architectures for Data Trusts
creator: Balambiga Ayappane, Rohith Vaidyanathan, Srinath Srinivasa, Jayati Deshmukh
description: Abstract Sensitive personal information of individuals and non-personal information of organizations or communities often needs to be legitimately exchanged among different stakeholders, to provide services, maintain public health, law and order, and so on. While such exchanges are necessary, they also impose enormous privacy and security challenges.

title: BRST invariant scalar and vector operators in the S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU\left(2\right)\times U\left(1\right) Higgs model
creator: D. Dudal, D.M. van Egmond, G. Peruzzo, S.P. Sorella
description: Abstract We present a set of BRST invariant composite operators in the S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU\left(2\right)\times U\left(1\right) Higgs model which exhibit an overlap with the observable scalar and vector particle states of the theory.

title: Isospectral Potentials and Quantum Mechanical Functions for Neutron-Neutron Scattering
creator: Anil Khachi
description: Abstract In this paper we have constructed inverse isospectral potentials for S 0 1 − n ​ n {}^{1}S_{0}-nn state by fitting the experimental SPS using Variational Monte-Carlo technique in tandem with PFM technique. The isospectral potentials are obtained such that the cost measure i.e.

title: MEM: Multi-Modal Elevation Mapping for Robotics and Learning
creator: Gian Erni, Jonas Frey, Takahiro Miki, Matias Mattamala, Marco Hutter
description: Abstract Elevation maps are commonly used to represent the environment of mobile robots and are instrumental for locomotion and navigation tasks. However, pure geometric information is insufficient for many field applications that require appearance or semantic information, which limits their applicability to other platforms or domains. In this work, we extend a 2.

title: Induced supersolidity in a Dy-Er mixture
creator: Soumyadeep Halder, Subrata Das, Sonjoy Majumder
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Soumyadeep Halder, Subrata Das, Sonjoy Majumder. Recent experimental realization of the heteronuclear dipolar mixture of Dy and Er atoms opens fascinating prospects for creating intriguing novel phases in dipolar quantum gases. The experimentally measured value of intra-species s s -wave scattering length of 166 Er condensate in a 164 Dy- 166 Er mixture is larger than its intra-species dipolar length, implies that the 166 Er condensate itself will not be in a regime of dominated dipole-dipole interaction (DDI).

title: Towards Sustainable Horizons: A Comprehensive Blueprint for Mars Colonization
creator: Florian Neukart
description: Abstract Establishing a human colony on Mars is one of the most ambitious endeavors of our time. This paper provides a comprehensive assessment of the challenges and solutions related to Mars colonization, emphasizing sustainability, efficiency, and the well-being of colonists.

title: Extraordinary physical properties of superconducting YBa 1.4 Sr 0.6 Cu 3 O 6 Se 0.51 in a multiphase ceramic material Journal: Materials Today
creator: V. Grinenko, A. Dudka, S. Nozaki, J. Kilcrease, A. Muto, J. Clarke, T. Hogan, V. Nikoghosyan, I. de Paiva, R. Dulal, S. Teknowijoyo, S. Chahid, A. Gulian
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by V. Grinenko, A. Dudka, S. Nozaki, J. Kilcrease, A. Muto, J. Clarke, T. Hogan, V. Nikoghosyan, I. de Paiva, R. Dulal, S. Teknowijoyo, S. Chahid, A. Gulian. We report on a novel material obtained by modifying pristine YBCO superconductor in solid phase synthesis via simultaneous partial substitution of Ba by Sr and O by Se.

title: Diquarks and Λ 0 / π + \Lambda^{0}/\pi^{+} , Ξ − / π + \Xi^{-}/\pi^{+} ratios in the framework of the EPNJL model
creator: A. V. Friesen, Yu. L. Kalinovsky
description: Abstract The applicability of the effective models to the description of baryons and the behaviour of ratios of strange baryons to pions is discussed. In the framework of the EPNJL model, the Bethe - Salpeter equation is used to find masses of baryons, which are considered as diquark-quark state.

title: Agent Co ordinatio n via C ontext u al R egression (AgentCONCUR) for Data Center Flexibility The author is with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.
creator: Vladimir Dvorkin, Member, IEEE
description: Abstract A network of spatially distributed data centers can provide operational flexibility to power systems by shifting computing tasks among electrically remote locations. However, harnessing this flexibility in real-time through the standard optimization techniques is challenged by the need for sensitive operational datasets and substantial computational resources.

title: Subset-Reach Estimation in Cross-Media Measurement
creator: Chenwei Wang, Jiayu Peng, Rieman Li, Ying Liu
description: Abstract We propose two novel approaches to address a critical problem of reach measurement across multiple media – how to estimate the reach of an unobserved subset of buying groups (BGs) based on the observed reach of other subsets of BGs. Specifically, we propose a model-free approach and a model-based approach.

title: A Lagrangian theory for galaxy shape statistics
creator: Nickolas Kokron
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nickolas Kokron. We formulate the Lagrangian perturbation theory of galaxy intrinsic alignments and compute the resulting auto and cross power spectra of galaxy shapes, densities and matter to 1-loop order. Our model represents a consistent effective-theory description of galaxy shape including the resummation of long-wavelength displacements which damp baryon acoustic oscillations, and includes one linear, three quadratic and two cubic dimensionless bias coefficients at this order, along with counterterms and stochastic contributions whose structure we derive.

title: ALMA Lensing Cluster Survey: average dust, gas, and star formation properties of cluster and field galaxies from stacking analysis 2021 ALMA Lensing Cluster Survey: average dust, gas, and star formation properties of cluster and field galaxies from stacking analysis – 11
creator: Guerrero, Andrea, Nagar, Neil, Kohno, Kotaro, Fujimoto, Seiji, Kokorev, Vasily, Brammer, Gabriel, Jolly, Jean-Baptiste, Knudsen, Kirsten, Sun, Fengwu, Bauer, Franz E, Caminha, Gabriel B, Caputi, Karina, Neumann, Gerald, Orellana-González, Gustavo, Cerulo, Pierluigi, González-López, Jorge, Laporte, N
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Guerrero, Andrea, Nagar, Neil, Kohno, Kotaro, Fujimoto, Seiji, Kokorev, Vasily, Brammer, Gabriel, Jolly, Jean-Baptiste, Knudsen, Kirsten, Sun, Fengwu, Bauer, Franz E, Caminha, Gabriel B, Caputi, Karina, Neumann, Gerald, Orellana-González, Gustavo, Cerulo, Pierluigi, González-López, Jorge, Laporte, N. We develop new tools for continuum and spectral stacking of ALMA data, and apply these to the ALMA Lensing Cluster Survey (ALCS).

title: Robust Safe Control with Multi-Modal Uncertainty
creator: Tianhao Wei, Liqian Ma, Ravi Pandya, Changliu Liu
description: Abstract Safety in dynamic systems with prevalent uncertainties is crucial. Current robust safe controllers, designed primarily for uni-modal uncertainties, may be either overly conservative or unsafe when handling multi-modal uncertainties. To address the problem, we introduce a novel framework for robust safe control, tailored to accommodate multi-modal Gaussian dynamics uncertainties and control limits.

title: Multi-Bellman operator for convergence of Q Q -learning with linear function approximation
creator: Diogo S. Carvalho, Pedro A. Santos, and Francisco S. Melo
description: Abstract We study the convergence of Q Q -learning with linear function approximation. Our key contribution is the introduction of a novel multi-Bellman operator that extends the traditional Bellman operator. By exploring the properties of this operator, we identify conditions under which the projected multi-Bellman operator becomes contractive, providing improved fixed-point guarantees compared to the Bellman operator.

title: Energy Optimal Control of a Harmonic Oscillator with a State Inequality Constraint
creator: Mi Zhou, Erik I Verriest, Chaouki Abdallah
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mi Zhou, Erik I Verriest, Chaouki Abdallah. In this article, the optimal control problem for a harmonic oscillator with an inequality constraint is considered. The applied energy of the oscillator during a fixed final time period is used as the performance criterion. The analytical solution with both small and large terminal time is found for a special case when the undriven oscillator system is initially at rest.

title: DeBERTinha: A Multistep Approach to Adapt DebertaV3 XSmall for Brazilian Portuguese Natural Language Processing Tasks
creator: Israel Campiotti 1, Matheus Rodrigues 2, Yuri Albuquerque 3, Rafael Azevedo, Alyson Andrade
description: Abstract This paper presents an approach for adapting the DebertaV3 XSmall model pre-trained in English for Brazilian Portuguese natural language processing (NLP) tasks. A key aspect of the methodology involves a multi-step training process to ensure the model is effectively tuned for the Portuguese language.

title: Electroweak Precision Measurements of a Nearly-Degenerate Z ′ Z^{\prime} - Z Z System
creator: Dayun Qiu, Yi-Lei Tang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dayun Qiu, Yi-Lei Tang. In this paper, we discuss the possibility to probe a nearly-degenerate Z ′ Z^{\prime} - Z Z system by analyzing the Z Z -lineshape at an electron-positron collider. Compared with the usual Z ′ Z^{\prime} in the literature well separated with the standard model (SM) Z Z boson in mass, the nearly-degenerate Z ′ Z^{\prime} - Z Z mixing affects the observed effective “oblique parameters” S ~ \tilde{S} , T ~ \tilde{T} , U ~ \tilde{U} , and the effective

title: Group rings and hyperbolic geometry
creator: Grigori Avramidi, Thomas Delzant
description: Abstract For a group acting on a hyperbolic space, we set up an algorithm in the group algebra showing that ideals generated by few elements are free, where few is a function of the minimal displacement of the action, and derive algebraic, geometric, and topological consequences. 1 Introduction Let G be a group and \mathbb{K} a field.

title: The fork and its role in unification of closure algebras
creator: Ivo Düntsch, Wojciech Dzik
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ivo Düntsch, Wojciech Dzik. We consider the two-pronged fork frame 𝙵 \mathtt{F} and the variety 𝐄𝐪 ⁡ ( B 𝙵 ) \Eq(B_{\mathtt{F}}) generated by its dual closure algebra B 𝙵 B_{\mathtt{F}} . We describe the finite projective algebras in 𝐄𝐪 ⁡ ( B 𝙵 ) \Eq(B_{\mathtt{F}}) and give a purely semantic proof that unification in 𝐄𝐪 ⁡ ( B 𝙵 ) \Eq(B_{\mathtt{F}}) is finitary.

title: Space-Time Attention with Shifted Non-Local Search
creator: Kent Gauen & Stanley Chan
description: Abstract Efficiently computing attention maps for videos is challenging due to the motion of objects between frames. While a standard non-local search is high-quality for a window surrounding each query point, the window’s small size cannot accommodate motion. Methods for long-range motion use an auxiliary network to predict the most similar key coordinates as offsets from each query location.

title: Measuring lepton number violation in heavy neutral lepton decays at the future muon collider
creator: Oleksii Mikulenko, Mariia Marinichenko
description: Abstract The future muon collider has the potential to discover feebly interacting particles in a wide range of masses above the electroweak scale. It is particularly suitable to search for heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), as their production cross section σ ∼ m W − 2 \sigma\sim m_{W}^{-2} is not suppressed by the new physics scale.

title: Hyperfine structure of the 𝐀 𝟏 ​ 𝚷 \mathbf{A^{1}\Pi} state of AlCl and its relevance to laser cooling and trapping
creator: John R. Daniel, Jamie C. Shaw, Chen Wang, Li-Ren Liu, Brian K. Kendrick, Boerge Hemmerling, Daniel J. McCarron
description: Abstract The majority of molecules proposed for laser cooling and trapping experiments have Σ \Sigma -type ground states. Specifically, Σ 2 {}^{2}\Sigma states have cycling transitions analogous to D 1 D_{1} -lines in alkali-metal atoms while Σ 1 {}^{1}\Sigma states offer both strong and weak cycling transitions analogous to those in alkaline-earth atoms.

title: Search for supersymmetry in final states with disappearing tracks in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
description: Abstract A search is presented for charged, long-lived supersymmetric particles in final states with one or more disappearing tracks. The search is based on data from proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC between 2016 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 137 \fbinv .

title: Local boundedness of minimizers under unbalanced Orlicz growth conditions
creator: Andrea Cianchi, Mathias Schäffner
description: Abstract . Local minimizers of integral functionals of the calculus of variations are analyzed under growth conditions dictated by different lower and upper bounds for the integrand. Growths of non-necessarily power type are allowed. The local boundedness of the relevant minimizers is established under a suitable balance between the lower and the upper bounds.

title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
creator: Chrisantha Fernando, Dylan Banarse, Henryk Michalewski, Simon Osindero, Tim Rocktäschel Google DeepMind {chrisantha,dylski,henrykm,osindero,rocktaschel}@google.com
description: Abstract Popular prompt strategies like Chain-of-Thought Prompting can dramatically improve the reasoning abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) in various domains. However, such hand-crafted prompt-strategies are often sub-optimal. In this paper, we present Promptbreeder , a general-purpose self-referential self-improvement mechanism that evolves and adapts prompts for a given domain.

title: Constant Approximation for Individual Preference Stable Clustering
creator: Anders Aamand, Justin Y. Chen, Allen Liu, Sandeep Silwal, Pattara Sukprasert, Ali Vakilian, Fred Zhang
description: Abstract Individual preference (IP) stability, introduced by Ahmadi et al. (ICML 2022), is a natural clustering objective inspired by stability and fairness constraints. A clustering is α \alpha -IP stable if the average distance of every data point to its own cluster is at most α \alpha times the average distance to any other cluster.

description: Abstract Supplementary Information 1 Determination of twist angle between the WSe {}_{2} and MoSe {}_{2} layers in heterostrucutres. The twist angle between the constituent layer of the heterostructure samples was determined by performing polarisation resolved second harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. Fig.

title: A genetic algorithm to search the space of Ehrhart h ∗ h^{*} -vectors
creator: Gabriele Balletti
description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gabriele Balletti. We describe a genetic algorithm to find candidates for h ∗ h^{*} -vectors satisfying given properties in the space of integers vectors of finite length. We use an implementation of such algorithm to find a 52-dimensional lattice polytope having a non-unimodal h ∗ h^{*} -vector which is the Cartesian product of two lattice polytopes having unimodal h ∗ h^{*} -vectors. This counterexample answers negatively to a question by Ferroni and Higashitani. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
